required_permission: existing Issues write; no scope expansion
resources: two newly created explicitly synthetic Issues
durable plan/checkpoint comments on Work Issue
steps: Write durable plan before any mutation; never use pre-existing business Issues as fixtures.
Create namespaced parent and child Issues once, preserving exact returned IDs and URLs; bodies specify cleanup and no real work.
Write exact created IDs to durable Work checkpoint before adding the edge.
Live-read parent sub-issues and child parent; reject unexpected existing relationship or visibility/marker mismatch.
GET parent sub-issues and child parent; prove exact edge in both directions.
Write mutation/readback receipt to durable Work before cleanup.
DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{parent_number}/sub_issue with sub_issue_id={child_id}; read back parent list and child parent.
Close both exact fixture Issues, preserve history/timeline, read back states and record durable cleanup receipt.
cleanup: Remove only the created sub-issue edge, then close the two created Issues. Keep plan, receipts and timeline; no deletion or history rewrite.
replay: Do not repeat create/add blindly. For a deliberate new experiment use a fresh namespace and new Issues; never reopen donor fixtures.
unknown_result: Stop dependent mutations. Live-read exact IDs and relationship endpoints; if a create response is lost, reconcile exact namespace through bounded complete issue enumeration and durable plan before retry. Incomplete/forbidden/ambiguous results stay UNKNOWN; no absence claim or retry.
durable_receipt_before_retry: Work Issue checkpoint with exact known resources, last known operation/result, uncertainty and reconciliation reads.
cleanup_failure: Keep resources identifiable and failure visible; write durable partial cleanup receipt before any separately justified retry. Do not erase failure evidence.
limits: No dependency edges, cycles, cross-repository/private behavior or production lifecycle
No induced network failure; UNKNOWN recovery path is a prescribed safety contract, not an executed fault injection
